_doc: Indicator registry for the Finland edition. One indicator = one entry in `indicators`. **The hard-data rule: every entry here is an official published figure or plain arithmetic on official figures — a difference, a share, a sum, a per-1,000. No entry may use an assumption, a fitted trend, a cap or a model of our own.** FIELDS — `key`: the id used in makro.json, the URL hash and the CSV export. `label` / `short` / `unit`: UI text. `level`: the finest geography the indicator natively exists at — 'kunta' | 'postinumero' | 'osa_alue'; a coarser value shown on a finer polygon is marked ° in the UI. `group`: which section of the indicator select it sits in (GROUP_ORDER in src/app.js: Demographics, Income & jobs, Housing stock, Market, Construction, Taxes, Safety, Outlook, Schools, Growth signals). `hue`: RGB target for the choropleth ramp (paper #E8EDE7 → hue). `fmt`: a key of FMT in src/app.js. `direction`: 'higher_better' | 'lower_better' | 'neutral' — which end of the scale is favourable; 'neutral' is never coloured good/bad and never carries the '↓ lower is better' note. `desc` / `note` / `warn`: the ⓘ details, the glossary line and the caveat. `chip: true` puts the indicator in the quick-pick chip row. SOURCES — `sources` is the list the fetcher pulls, one entry per level: {`src`: 'statfin' | 'paavo' | 'aluesarjat' | 'kela' | 'vero' | 'hri', `table`: '<db>/<id>' for StatFin (e.g. 'ashi/13mt'), `vars`: {<variable code>: [<value codes>]} exactly as the PxWeb metadata spells them, `geo`: the level this source serves, `area_var`: the PxWeb variable holding the area code, `contents`: the contentscode value the number comes from}. A variable left out of `vars` is returned as its total only when the PxWeb metadata says elimination=true — scripts/validate_config.py checks that for every entry. `src_verify` is the list behind the 'Verify at source' link; each entry carries `geo`, and either `table` ('<db>/<id>', which becomes the pxdata.stat.fi table page) or a full `url` for a file source. VINTAGES — a StatFin area variable carries its classification year in its own name (`postinumeroalue_4_20220101`, `alue_2026`). It is recorded verbatim in `vars`, and two tables on different vintages are never joined silently: docs/GEO.md lists which vintage each table is on and what we do about it. CALCS — `calc` names the post-processing in scripts/build_makro.py: 'passthrough', 'share_of_total', 'yoy_pct', 'per_1000_dwellings', 'ratio_pct', 'sum4q', 'rolling4q_per_1000_pop', 'rolling4q_per_1000_dwellings', 'rolling4q_yoy_pct', 'forecast'. `select` narrows the rows a calc sees; a value may be a list of codes, in which case matching rows are summed. `history_from` is the first year of the yearly history in Charts; `map_from` the first year the map/table year selector offers. SUPPRESSION — Paavo suppresses areas under 30 residents / 10 households and StatFin's ashi and asvu suppress cells with too few observations. A suppressed cell is null and is shown as '–'. It is never read as 0, and an area we do not cover reads 'Not covered yet' rather than a number. A source entry may carry `cells`: {published code: the indicator's code}, for when the same figure is spelled differently in two tables — ashi/13mt names blocks of flats by room count while ashi/13mx names them 3, and neither table is wrong. A source with `src: "csv"` reads a committed file written by one of the scripts/import_*.py scripts, naming its own columns (area_col, period_col, code_col or `as`, value_col).

indicators.label: Population growth
indicators.desc: Change in the number of inhabitants over one year, %. Kunta figures are Statistics Finland's population statistics at 31 December; postal-code figures are Paavo, which runs two years behind.
indicators.note: Kunta and postal-code growth come from two different releases and two different years. Each level's own period is shown in the 'as of' line; they are never averaged together.
indicators.warn: Paavo's statistics year lags its release by two years: the 2026 release carries 2024 figures.

indicators.label: Median income of inhabitants
indicators.desc: Median disposable monetary income of inhabitants aged 18 or over (Paavo hr_mtu).
indicators.note: Paavo, Statistics Finland's postal-code statistics. The same definitions are used at kunta and postinumero level, so the two are directly comparable. Paavo suppresses an area with fewer than 30 residents or 10 households — a suppressed figure is shown as – and is never read as zero.
indicators.warn: Paavo's statistics year lags its release by two years: the 2026 release carries 2024 figures.

indicators.label: Unemployment rate
indicators.desc: Unemployed as a share of the labour force, where the labour force is the employed plus the unemployed (Paavo pt_tyott ÷ (pt_tyoll + pt_tyott)). Paavo publishes the counts, not the rate; the division is ours and is plain arithmetic on the two published cells.
indicators.note: Paavo, Statistics Finland's postal-code statistics. The same definitions are used at kunta and postinumero level, so the two are directly comparable. Paavo suppresses an area with fewer than 30 residents or 10 households — a suppressed figure is shown as – and is never read as zero.

indicators.note: Paavo, Statistics Finland's postal-code statistics. The same definitions are used at kunta and postinumero level, so the two are directly comparable. Paavo suppresses an area with fewer than 30 residents or 10 households — a suppressed figure is shown as – and is never read as zero.

indicators.note: Paavo, Statistics Finland's postal-code statistics. The same definitions are used at kunta and postinumero level, so the two are directly comparable. indicators.note: Paavo, Statistics Finland's postal-code statistics. The same definitions are used at kunta and postinumero level, so the two are directly comparable. indicators.label: Foreign-language speakers
indicators.desc: Inhabitants whose registered mother tongue is neither a national language (Finnish, Swedish or Sami) nor unknown, as a share of the population — Statistics Finland's published 'FOREIGN LANGUAGES, TOTAL' (code 02) divided by the population total.
indicators.note: Published only per kunta. Postal areas and osa-alueet show the kunta figure, marked °. Language is the one registered in the population information system, which is not the same as country of birth or citizenship.

indicators.label: Unemployment rate, monthly
indicators.desc: Unemployed jobseekers as a share of the labour force, published monthly by the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Employment's employment service statistics. This is a different definition from the annual Paavo rate and the two are not comparable.
indicators.note: TEM counts registered unemployed jobseekers at the end of the month. Statistics Finland's Labour Force Survey and Paavo's register-based rate both differ from it — never read the two rates as the same number measured twice.
indicators.warn: A different definition from the annual rate above. Compare month to month, not to Paavo.

indicators.label: Housing-allowance households
indicators.desc: Households receiving general housing allowance (yleinen asumistuki) as a share of all household-dwelling units. Kela publishes the recipient count; the denominator is Paavo's household total for the same kunta, and the division is plain arithmetic on two published cells.
indicators.source: Kela, yleinen asumistuki, saajaruokakunnat kunnittain (avoindata.suomi.fi, CC BY 4.0) · denominator Tilastokeskus Paavo 12f8 te_taly
indicators.note: Kela counts recipient households (saajaruokakunta) at the end of the month; Paavo counts household-dwelling units (asuntokunta) at 31 December. The two are close but not identical concepts, so read the share as an order of magnitude, not a precise ratio.
indicators.warn: Kela's monthly recipient count and Paavo's annual household count are different concepts measured at different dates.

indicators.label: Old flats, price per m²
indicators.desc: Average price per square metre of old dwellings in housing companies (kerrostalo, all room counts), from realised transactions. The yearly figure is the published annual one; the quarterly series behind the Yearly | Quarterly toggle is the publisher's own quarterly table.
indicators.note: ashi publishes the arithmetic mean price per square metre and the number of sales for every building-type class. A class total is the sales-weighted mean of its classes — exactly the arithmetic mean over the underlying transactions, since the weight is each class's own transaction count. No class is estimated: a suppressed class is left out of both sums and the area reads – when nothing is left. At kunta level the same figure comes from 13mx, whose building-type classification differs (0 = all types, 1 = terraced, 3 = blocks of flats); the blocks-of-flats class is used, so the two levels mean the same thing.
indicators.warn: Postal-code prices are published on the 2022 postal-code classification (1 724 areas), while the map is drawn on the 2026 one (3 018 areas). Only areas whose code exists in both carry a price; the rest read – rather than a neighbour's figure.

indicators.label: Sales of old flats
indicators.desc: Number of realised transactions behind the price above (kerrostalo, all room counts). A price is only as good as the count under it, so the two are always shown together.
indicators.source: Tilastokeskus ashi 13mu / 13mt / 13mx (asset transfer tax data from 2020)
indicators.note: Counts come from asset transfer tax data from 2020 onwards (lkm_julk20). Where the publisher suppressed a class, that class is missing from the count as well as from the price.
indicators.warn: Postal-code prices are published on the 2022 postal-code classification (1 724 areas), while the map is drawn on the 2026 one (3 018 areas). Only areas whose code exists in both carry a price; the rest read – rather than a neighbour's figure.

indicators.label: Terraced houses, price per m²
indicators.desc: Average price per square metre of old terraced houses (rivitalo) in housing companies.
indicators.note: Terraced houses are far fewer transactions than flats, so this is suppressed in many areas. A missing figure means too few sales to publish, not cheap housing.
indicators.warn: Postal-code prices are published on the 2022 postal-code classification (1 724 areas), while the map is drawn on the 2026 one (3 018 areas). Only areas whose code exists in both carry a price; the rest read – rather than a neighbour's figure.

indicators.label: Free-market rent
indicators.desc: Average rent per square metre per month for non-subsidised (vapaarahoitteiset) rental dwellings, all room counts, from the publisher's quarterly rent statistics.
indicators.note: Published for 27 municipalities and for every maakunta. A kunta with no figure of its own shows its maakunta's, marked ^ — that is a regional average, not a measurement of that municipality.
indicators.warn: Postal-code rents (asvu 13eb) were discontinued: the last quarter ever published is 2025Q4. This kunta-level series is the live replacement, and the two are not the same geography.

indicators.label: Rent observations
indicators.desc: Number of rental dwellings behind the rent above. A rent from a handful of dwellings is not the same fact as a rent from thousands.
indicators.note: Where the rent is inherited from the maakunta (^), so is this count.

indicators.label: Government-subsidised (ARA) rent
indicators.desc: Average rent per square metre per month for government-subsidised (arava- and korkotuki-financed, 'ARA') rental dwellings, all room counts.
indicators.note: The funding code for government-subsidised rents is 2 in this table and 0 in the discontinued archive table — the codes are inverted between them, so the two must never be spliced by code.

indicators.label: Rent change, year on year
indicators.desc: Annual change of the rent index for non-subsidised rental dwellings, as published (2025 = 100). Not computed here — this is the publisher's own figure.
indicators.source: Tilastokeskus asvu 15fa, annual change of the rent index
indicators.note: The index was rebased to 2025 = 100. Its level is not comparable with the older 2015 = 100 series without chaining, which this dashboard does not do.

indicators.label: Free-market rent by postal code (discontinued)
indicators.desc: Average rent per square metre per month for non-subsidised rental dwellings by postal code area. Statistics Finland stopped publishing this table; the last quarter is 2025Q4 and there will be no more. It is kept because nothing replaces it below kunta level, and it is labelled with its own end date everywhere it appears.
indicators.note: Room-count classes are combined as a mean weighted by each class's own number of observations — the same arithmetic as the price above. The table covers 580 postal areas, a third of the price table's and a fifth of Paavo's.
indicators.warn: Last published 2025Q4 — series discontinued by publisher. Statistics Finland stopped publishing rents by postal code; nothing replaces them below kunta level, so the frozen series is kept and labelled. It is never extended and never blended with the live kunta-level rent.

indicators.label: Dwellings with no permanent residents
indicators.desc: Dwellings with no permanent residents as a share of the whole dwelling stock (asunnot joissa ei vakituisia asukkaita ÷ kaikki asunnot).
indicators.note: A dwelling with no permanent residents may be a holiday home, a second home, a dwelling between tenancies or genuinely empty. The statistic does not separate them.
indicators.warn: One year only: this table publishes 2025 and nothing earlier. There is no history.

indicators.label: Net migration
indicators.desc: Total net migration — intermunicipal net migration plus net immigration — per 1 000 inhabitants. The numerator is the publisher's own 'total net migration' cell; the division by population is ours.
indicators.note: Per 1 000 inhabitants of the same year, using the population cell published in the same table, so numerator and denominator always come from one release.

indicators.label: Intermunicipal net migration
indicators.desc: Net migration between Finnish municipalities only, per 1 000 inhabitants — the part of the flow that is people moving within Finland.
indicators.note: Shown beside total net migration so the domestic and international parts of the flow can be told apart instead of being read as one number.

indicators.label: Dwellings completed
indicators.desc: New dwellings completed in the last twelve months per 1 000 existing dwellings. The numerator is the publisher's own moving annual total.
indicators.source: Tilastokeskus raku 156f (building and dwelling production, monthly, by region)
indicators.note: **Published by maakunta only.** Statistics Finland publishes no municipal building and dwelling production at all — the discontinued ras tables were regional too. Every kunta therefore shows its maakunta's rate, marked ^. It is a regional rate, not that municipality's own construction. The denominator is the dwelling stock published by Paavo for the same maakunta (the sum of its kunnat's published stocks), latest year.
indicators.warn: Maakunta level. Two municipalities in the same maakunta always show the same number.

indicators.label: Dwellings started
indicators.desc: New dwellings started in the last twelve months per 1 000 existing dwellings (publisher's moving annual total).
indicators.note: Maakunta level — see 'Dwellings completed'. Starts lead completions by roughly one to two years, which is why both are shown. The denominator is the dwelling stock published by Paavo for the same maakunta (the sum of its kunnat's published stocks), latest year.
indicators.warn: Maakunta level. Two municipalities in the same maakunta always show the same number.

indicators.label: Dwellings permitted
indicators.desc: New dwellings granted a building permit in the last twelve months per 1 000 existing dwellings (publisher's moving annual total).
indicators.note: Maakunta level — see 'Dwellings completed'. A permit is the earliest published signal of future supply; not every permit is built. The denominator is the dwelling stock published by Paavo for the same maakunta (the sum of its kunnat's published stocks), latest year.
indicators.warn: Maakunta level. Two municipalities in the same maakunta always show the same number.

indicators.label: Property tax, permanent dwelling
indicators.desc: Kiinteistöveroprosentti for a building in permanent residential use (vakituisen asumisen %) — the rate that applies to an ordinary home.
indicators.note: The applied percentage as published by Verohallinto, not an effective rate: what an owner actually pays also depends on the taxable value of the property, which this dashboard does not carry. The 2026 column is the publisher's own preliminary figure (ennakkotieto). Lower is better is read from an owner's side — a lower rate is a lower holding cost. It is not a judgement about the municipality: the same rate funds its services.

indicators.label: Property tax, other dwelling
indicators.desc: Kiinteistöveroprosentti for a residential building not in permanent use (muun kuin vakituisen asumisen %) — holiday homes and second homes.
indicators.note: The applied percentage as published by Verohallinto, not an effective rate: what an owner actually pays also depends on the taxable value of the property, which this dashboard does not carry. The 2026 column is the publisher's own preliminary figure (ennakkotieto). Lower is better is read from an owner's side — a lower rate is a lower holding cost. It is not a judgement about the municipality: the same rate funds its services.

indicators.label: Property tax, general (building)
indicators.desc: Yleinen kiinteistövero-% for buildings — the rate for everything the specific categories do not cover.
indicators.note: The applied percentage as published by Verohallinto, not an effective rate: what an owner actually pays also depends on the taxable value of the property, which this dashboard does not carry. The 2026 column is the publisher's own preliminary figure (ennakkotieto). Lower is better is read from an owner's side — a lower rate is a lower holding cost. It is not a judgement about the municipality: the same rate funds its services.

indicators.label: Property tax, general (land)
indicators.desc: Yleinen kiinteistövero-% for land (maapohja).
indicators.note: The applied percentage as published by Verohallinto, not an effective rate: what an owner actually pays also depends on the taxable value of the property, which this dashboard does not carry. The 2026 column is the publisher's own preliminary figure (ennakkotieto). Lower is better is read from an owner's side — a lower rate is a lower holding cost. It is not a judgement about the municipality: the same rate funds its services.

indicators.label: Property tax, undeveloped building site
indicators.desc: Rakentamattoman rakennuspaikan % — the higher rate a municipality may set on a zoned but unbuilt plot. Where it is high, the municipality is pushing owners to build.
indicators.note: The applied percentage as published by Verohallinto, not an effective rate: what an owner actually pays also depends on the taxable value of the property, which this dashboard does not carry. The 2026 column is the publisher's own preliminary figure (ennakkotieto). Lower is better is read from an owner's side — a lower rate is a lower holding cost. It is not a judgement about the municipality: the same rate funds its services.
indicators.warn: Not every municipality sets this rate; where none is set the figure is missing, which is not the same as a rate of zero.

indicators.label: Municipal income tax
indicators.desc: Kunnallisveroprosentti — the municipal income tax rate, as decided by the municipality and published by Verohallinto.
indicators.note: Rates fell sharply in 2023 when health and social services moved to the hyvinvointialueet and the state took the funding with them — a 2022 rate and a 2023 rate are not comparable, and this series starts at the current decision. Lower is better is read from an owner's side — a lower rate is a lower holding cost. It is not a judgement about the municipality: the same rate funds its services.
indicators.warn: One year only: Verohallinto publishes the rate as an annual decision, not as a time series, so there is no history here.

indicators.label: Projected population change 2026→2040
indicators.desc: Projected change in the number of inhabitants from 2026 to 2040, %. Both figures are cells of Väestöennuste 2024; the percentage between them is plain arithmetic.

proj.caveat: A projection is a calculation of what the population would be if the observed trends in births, deaths and migration continued. It is the publisher's scenario, not a forecast of what will happen, and it takes no account of housing policy, zoning or a new employer arriving.

indicators.note: Väestöennuste 2024, published 2024-10-24. One vintage, not a series: there is no history to scroll through, and the figure does not change until Tilastokeskus publishes a new projection. The projected part of every chart is drawn dashed.

indicators.label: Reported offences
indicators.desc: All offences against the penal code, per 1 000 inhabitants — the publisher's own rate, not a division of ours.
indicators.source: Tilastokeskus rpk 13h4 (offences per 1 000 population in the area)
indicators.note: Offences known to the police, counted **where the offence happened** and divided by the population **registered there** — the publisher's own words. A city centre with a large daytime and visitor population therefore carries offences committed against people who do not live there. Read it as where crime is recorded, not as how dangerous residents' own lives are. Published per kunta only: postal areas and osa-alueet show the kunta figure, marked °. About a quarter of this total is traffic offences, which say as much about enforcement as about a neighbourhood; the thematic rates below are the ones to compare areas on.
indicators.warn: Published per kunta only. Finland publishes no open crime data below municipality level.

indicators.label: Sea flood hazard zone — 1/100a
indicators.desc: Share of the area's land inside Suomen ympäristökeskus's sea flood hazard zone for a flood with a 1-in-100-year return period (meritulva 1/100a). The return period is the publisher's, not a horizon we chose: it is a recurrence probability, not a forecast for a particular year.
indicators.note: Measured from Suomen ympäristökeskus's own flood-hazard polygons at 25 m per pixel: the publisher's classes are rendered flat and counted inside this area's land, and the share is that count divided by the area's land. The zones are published as millions of raster-derived fragments (3.4 M and 4.0 M features for the two 1/100a layers) and cannot be fetched as vectors at a usable size — the method and why are in docs/CLIMATE_FI.md.
indicators.warn: SYKE flood-maps designated areas, not the whole country. An area with no figure is NOT MAPPED, which is not the same as no flood hazard. The Flood-mapped row says how much of the area has been assessed. Screening indicators for comparing areas, not a property-level risk assessment.

indicators.label: Flood-mapped share of the area
indicators.desc: Share of the area's land that Suomen ympäristökeskus has flood-mapped at all. **This is a coverage figure, not a hazard figure.** Where it is 0 the area has not been assessed and the flood rows above are blank; where it is high, a 0 in those rows means a real 0.
indicators.note: Taken from SYKE's own `kuiva maa` class — the dry land inside its mapped area — together with every flood class, so it is the publisher's own statement of what it has assessed, not an inference from where zones happen to be.
indicators.warn: SYKE flood-maps designated areas, not the whole country. An area with no figure is NOT MAPPED, which is not the same as no flood hazard. The Flood-mapped row says how much of the area has been assessed.

indicators.label: Radon, mean
indicators.desc: Mean indoor radon concentration measured by STUK in detached houses (pientalot) in this area. Finland's mean is 228 Bq/m³ and the action level for a dwelling is 300 Bq/m³.
indicators.note: Measured in detached houses only, so it describes the ground and the low-rise stock that sits on it — not a flat in a block. STUK's own blanks are suppressed figures, not zeros, and stay blank here.
indicators.warn: Measurements are voluntary, so the sample is not a random sample of dwellings. Screening indicators for comparing areas, not a property-level risk assessment.

indicators.label: Radon, median
indicators.desc: Median measured indoor radon concentration in detached houses. The median is well below the mean everywhere, because the distribution has a long upper tail.
indicators.note: As above; STUK publishes both, and both are carried.
indicators.warn: Measurements are voluntary, so the sample is not a random sample of dwellings. Screening indicators for comparing areas, not a property-level risk assessment.

indicators.label: Radon over 300 Bq/m³
indicators.desc: Share of STUK's measurements in this area above 300 Bq/m³, the action level for an existing dwelling in Finnish regulation (STUK).
indicators.note: Blank where STUK suppressed the figure — typically an area with too few measurements. A blank is not a zero.
indicators.warn: Measurements are voluntary, so the sample is not a random sample of dwellings. Screening indicators for comparing areas, not a property-level risk assessment.

indicators.label: Transport projects under way or decided
indicators.desc: Major transport projects that are under construction, decided or under study and whose published alignment touches this area.
indicators.source: Väylävirasto — hanketiedot (CC BY 4.0), plus the curated major projects in data/external/infra_fi.csv
indicators.note: Counted over **major** projects only — every curated project, and every Väylävirasto project the agency itself gave a project page (46 of its 267). Its list runs down to repainting a single bridge, and a repaint is not a growth signal. Projects already finished are not counted either.
indicators.warn: A count of projects, not of investment: the agency publishes no cost estimate in its project layers, so a tunnel and a junction weigh the same. Read it as 'something is being built here', not as a measure of how much.

indicators.label: Transport projects within 1.2 km
indicators.desc: Major transport projects whose published alignment lies inside this area or within 1 200 m of it — roughly a fifteen-minute walk, the distance at which a new line or junction starts to matter to an address.
indicators.source: Väylävirasto — hanketiedot (CC BY 4.0), plus the curated major projects in data/external/infra_fi.csv
indicators.note: Counted over **major** projects only — every curated project, and every Väylävirasto project the agency itself gave a project page (46 of its 267). Its list runs down to repainting a single bridge, and a repaint is not a growth signal. Projects already finished are not counted either. The 1 200 m buffer is measured in degrees of latitude, which in Finland reaches slightly further east–west than 1 200 m — the conservative direction.
indicators.warn: A count of projects, not of investment: the agency publishes no cost estimate in its project layers, so a tunnel and a junction weigh the same. Read it as 'something is being built here', not as a measure of how much.

indicators.label: Dwellings in buildings built before 1980
indicators.desc: Dwellings in buildings the register records as completed before 1980, as a share of the dwellings in buildings whose completion year it publishes. 1980 is a cut, not a threshold of quality: it is simply a round year before the 1980s and 1990s stock.
indicators.note: Counted over the register's own buildings with at least 2 dwellings — the register also carries saunas, sheds and bell towers, and a housing figure that counted those would not be a housing figure. 250 785 of 3 799 740 buildings qualify. It is a share of dwellings, not of buildings.
indicators.warn: Buildings whose completion year the register does not publish are left out of both the numerator and the denominator, rather than counted as new.

indicators.label: Floor area per dwelling
indicators.desc: The register's published gross floor area (kerrosala) of a building divided by the number of dwellings in it, summed over the area. A building average — the register publishes no per-dwelling area and no room counts, so this is not a measurement of any one dwelling and includes stairwells and common space.
indicators.note: Counted over the register's own buildings with at least 2 dwellings — the register also carries saunas, sheds and bell towers, and a housing figure that counted those would not be a housing figure. 250 785 of 3 799 740 buildings qualify. It is a share of dwellings, not of buildings.
indicators.warn: Gross floor area includes stairwells and common space, so it is larger than the living area a dwelling advertises. Not comparable with the Ø dwelling size from Paavo, which is living area.

osa._doc: The osa-alue layer's indicators are NOT registered here: they are built by scripts/build_osa.py, because every one of them is a share computed from one Aluesarjat table and the registry's source/calc shape would only restate the script. The layer's registry travels with its data in data/processed/osa_alue.json. Aluesarjat is open for both non-commercial and commercial use; the condition is an attribution naming the database and the underlying source, which the layer carries in the UI and in docs/SOURCES.md.

_calcs.share_pct: sum(num) / sum(den) * 100 — both from the same table, area and period
_calcs.ratio_pct: sum(num) / sum(den) * 100 where den is a list that includes num (a rate whose denominator the publisher does not publish, e.g. unemployed / (employed + unemployed))
_calcs.weighted_mean: Σ(num[i] × weight[i]) ÷ Σ(weight[i]) — a mean weighted by each class's own published count, which is exact when num is itself a mean per unit
_calcs.per_1000_dwellings: Σ(num) ÷ the area's dwelling stock × 1000; the stock is Paavo's latest published count for that area
_calcs.per_1000: Σ(num) ÷ Σ(den) × 1000, both from the same table, area and period
_calcs.proj_growth: (pop[to] / pop[from] - 1) × 100 on the projection's own cells
_calcs.proj_rate_5y: (pop[from+5] - pop[from]) ÷ 5 ÷ pop[from] × 1000 — residents per 1 000 per year
_calcs.proj_group: (group[to] / group[from] - 1) × 100 for the age band named by `group_key`
_calcs.proj_share_rel: the area's group share at `to` minus Finland's, in percentage points
